chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, raised the hadith, saying:

Abu Umamah, a companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), was saying: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Four [qualities] in which if one is found, his earnings are good: when he buys, he does not fault [the goods]; and when he sells, he does not praise [them excessively]; and he does not conceal defects; and in between that, he does not swear oaths.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four conditions for pure earnings in Islamic trade according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual purity of trade by emphasizing honesty and moderation in commercial interactions, a core tenet of Shia commercial jurisprudence. The four conditions—avoiding nitpicking when buying, refraining from boastful praise when selling, concealing no defects, and minimizing oaths—ensure that transactions are free from deception and excessive worldly attachment. This framework aligns with the Prophetic tradition of treating commerce as an act of worship when conducted with integrity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, raising the Hadeeth, said,

‘Abu Amama, a companion of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was saying, ‘I heard Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saying: ‘If four things happen to be in someone, so his earnings are good – whenever he buyes, he does not fault (the merchandise to have its price reduced); and whenever he sells, he does not praise (the merchandise to get it sold); and he does not cheat (conceal defects of the merchandise being sold); and in what is between that, he does not swear oaths (to get the merchandise sold or bought)’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa in a marfu’ manner’ has said the following:

“Abu ’Amamah, a companion of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘I heard the Messenger of Allah saying, “One who has four things his earning is fine: When buying does not belittle the merchandise, when selling does not admire the merchandise, does not adulterate and in between does not swear.’””
